sections.h2: What does a Rahway seller need to arrange before closing?
sections.html:
Rahway issues a Certificate of Approval for Continued Occupancy, called a CACO, whenever ownership changes, and the Fire Prevention Bureau separately inspects the house for smoke alarms, carbon monoxide alarms and an extinguisher. Both items belong on your calendar the day a contract is signed.

Rahway is a compact Union County city of about 3.9 square miles of land, so the city's inspection checklist reaches nearly every sale. The sections below cover the numbers, the local rules and the state filings that follow.

sections.h2: How big is Rahway and what do its housing numbers show?
sections.html:
Rahway counted 29,556 residents in 2020, and the Census Bureau estimates 31,010 for July 1, 2025. About half of its households own, and the city packs roughly 7,586 people into each square mile of land.

sections.h2: How did Rahway grow and where does the river run?
sections.html:
The Lenape lived here first. In January 1777 colonial forces defeated British troops at the Battle of Spanktown, named after the city's original settler name, Spanktown. Rahway grew along the stagecoach and railroad routes between New York and Philadelphia, and the navigable Rahway River helped its factories. The legislature made it a city on April 19, 1858, and the first council met on May 3 of that year.

The river enters from Clark, takes in Robinsons Branch near Elizabeth Avenue and the South Branch near East Hazlewood Avenue, then leaves toward Linden and Woodbridge and drains into the Arthur Kill. Inman Heights and North Rahway are named sections of the city. Ask the Building Department for the flood status of your lot if your street is near the water, since buyers and insurers will ask for it.

sections.h2: How have downtown and Merck changed the Rahway economy?
sections.html:
After postwar factory closures hollowed out the center, the city began a downtown revitalization plan in the late 1990s that added market-rate housing, a hotel, galleries and shops. The old Rahway Theatre reopened as the Union County Performing Arts Center after a $6.2 million renovation, and the American Planning Association named downtown a Great Downtown in 2020.

Merck is the largest private employer in the city. It returned its global headquarters to its Rahway research campus, completing the move in 2024. The Watt Hotel opened across from the train station in 2019 with 100 rooms inside a 17-story building.

  • Census data for 2022 shows about $283 million in retail sales in Rahway.
  • The same data shows $229 million in health care and social assistance receipts and about $87 million in accommodation and food service sales.

sections.h2: How do trains and highways serve Rahway?
sections.html:
Rahway station is on NJ Transit's North Jersey Coast Line and Northeast Corridor Line, and a typical ride to New York Penn Station takes 38 minutes. A 524-space parking deck opened across from the station in January 2005. NJ Transit route 115 reaches the Port Authority Bus Terminal and route 48 reaches Elizabeth and Perth Amboy.

US 1/9, Route 27 and Route 35 serve the city, and the Garden State Parkway and the New Jersey Turnpike each lie about two miles outside its limits. Newark Liberty International Airport is 10.2 miles northeast, roughly a 20-minute drive.

sections.h2: Which schools and parks serve Rahway homeowners?
sections.html:
Rahway Public Schools enrolled 4,311 students in 2024-25 across six schools: Grover Cleveland, Franklin, Madison and Roosevelt elementary schools, the Rahway 7th and 8th Grade Academy, and Rahway High School with 1,286 students.

The city has more than ten parks. Rahway River Park, which Union County maintains and which extends into Clark, has the Walter E. Ulrich pool, renovated and retiled in 2021. City government follows the Faulkner Act mayor-council plan adopted in 1955, with a nine-member council.

sections.h2: What does the Rahway CACO inspection cover and cost?
sections.html:
The Property Maintenance Division in the Department of Code Enforcement accepts the Application for Certificates of Approval for Continued Occupancy. You check the change of ownership box, list the closing date and give seller and buyer contact details. The 2025 form lists $100 per residential unit for a CACO and $100 per unit for a temporary CACO. Commercial or industrial units cost $200, and a rental built before 1978 costs $125 and is subject to dust wipes.

Properties with two or more units, and commercial or mixed-use buildings, must first obtain a zoning permit and a Fire Department approval. A temporary CACO is possible once all fire prevention measures are met and the buyer signs an affidavit agreeing to handle the rest.

The city's list of common concerns tells you what to fix in advance:

  • Foundations, roofs, porches and stairs must be sound, with no open cracks or leaks.
  • Stairs with more than four risers need a handrail 30 to 42 inches high.
  • Windows need working glazing and screens on openings used for ventilation.
  • Habitable rooms need two outlets, kitchens need three, and any outlet within six feet of water needs ground fault protection.
  • Cellars and crawl spaces must be free of dampness, and drains must run clear.
  • Peeling paint, loose plaster and decayed wood on interior surfaces must be corrected.

sections.h2: What does the Rahway fire inspection look for?
sections.html:
The Fire Prevention Bureau inspects single-family houses when a smoke detector compliance certificate is requested for a sale. A fire safety inspection also accompanies a change in ownership. The city's guidance sets these standards:

  • One smoke alarm on every level, basements included, and none farther than 10 feet from a bedroom door.
  • Battery units must carry sealed 10-year batteries, hard-wired alarms cannot be swapped for battery types, and no alarm may be more than 10 years old.
  • A carbon monoxide alarm within 10 feet of sleeping areas.
  • One extinguisher rated at least 2A:10BC, no heavier than 10 pounds, mounted within 10 feet of the kitchen and no more than 12 years old.

Replace expired alarms before you book the inspection so a failed visit does not push back closing.

sections.h2: What state forms and fees follow a Rahway sale?
sections.html:
The deed is recorded with the Union County Clerk, whose record room holds land transactions from 1857 forward and whose Elizabeth recording office takes documents over the counter on weekdays.

Gross Income Tax forms depend on who is selling. A New Jersey resident individual, estate or trust signs the GIT/REP-3. A nonresident seller files the GIT/REP-1 at closing, with an estimated payment calculated as the gain times 10.75%, and never less than 2% of the consideration in the deed. The county clerk forwards that payment to the state. An out-of-state heir selling an inherited Rahway house should plan for this withholding.

faqs.q: Does Rahway require an inspection before a house sale?
faqs.a: Yes. A CACO is needed when ownership changes, and the Fire Prevention Bureau inspects single-family houses when a smoke detector compliance certificate is requested for a sale. Apply early so both inspections fit before closing.

faqs.q: How much is a Rahway CACO for a residential sale?
faqs.a: The 2025 application lists $100 per residential unit for a CACO and $100 per unit for a temporary CACO. A rental built before 1978 costs $125 per unit and receives dust wipes during inspection.

faqs.q: Can I close in Rahway with repairs still unfinished?
faqs.a: Possibly. A temporary CACO is available when all fire prevention measures are completed and the buyer endorses an affidavit agreeing to address the remaining inspection items. Properties with two or more units need zoning and Fire Department approval first.

faqs.q: What must a nonresident Rahway seller pay at closing?
faqs.a: A nonresident files the GIT/REP-1 and makes an estimated Gross Income Tax payment equal to the gain times 10.75%, subject to a 2% of consideration minimum. The payment goes through the county clerk with the deed.

faqs.q: Where can I look up Rahway property records?
faqs.a: The Union County Clerk's online land records search lets you search by name, book and page, instrument number or date range, and the record room in Elizabeth holds land transactions from 1857 to the present.
